safi-cedvel:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is the wāw of the oath. (الذاريات) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is أقسم ("I swear"). (ذروا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governing element being الذاريات. (الفاء) is a conjunction in the three places. (وقرا) is the direct object of the active participle الحاملات. (يسرا) is an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective [Note: or it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "easily moving".]. (أمرا) is the direct object of the active participle المقسّمات. (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the ism of انّ [Note: and it is then good to separate (انّ) and (ما) in the written form ... It is also possible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is the ism of انّ.], and the returning pronoun is omitted; the (الواو) in (توعدون) is the deputy agent. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, a substitute for the shifted lām, giving emphasis, in both places.
Clause: «(أقسم) بالذاريات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
And the clause: «توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «إنّ ما توعدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «إنّ الدين لواقع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.

* Morphology:
(الذاريات) is the plural of الذارية, the feminine of الذاري, an active participle from the triliteral ذرا يذرو, on the pattern فاعل. It underwent ʿilāl by substitution; its origin was الذارو, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ because what precedes it has a kasra.. It is also possible that the verb is ذرى يذري of the bāb of ضرب, in which case there is no ʿilāl.
(ذروا) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb ذرا يذرو, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa and then sukūn.
(الحاملات) is the plural of الحاملة, the feminine of الحامل, an active participle from the triliteral حمل, on the pattern فاعل.
(وقرا) is a noun meaning "load", i.e. what is carried; its pattern is فعل with kasra and then sukūn.
(المقسّمات) is the plural of المقسّمة, the feminine of المقسّم, an active participle from the quadriliteral (form II) قسّم, on the pattern مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الدين) is a noun meaning "recompense"; its pattern is فعل with kasra and then sukūn.. See also verse (4) of Sūrat al-Fātiḥa.

safi-cedvel:7-9.t:
* I'rab:
(والسماء) is like والذاريات. (ذات) is an adjective of السماء, genitive. (اللام) is the lām of the oath. (في قول) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (عنه) is attached to (يؤفك). (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a deputy agent; and the deputy agent of the verb (أفك) is a latent pronoun (ḍamīr mustatir) that is the returning pronoun.
Clause: «(أقسم) بالسماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّكم لفي قول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «يؤفك عنه من أفك» is in the position of the genitive, a second adjective of قول [Note: This holds if the pronoun in (عنه) refers back to القول ... It may refer to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and then the clause is resumptive.].
And the clause: «أفك» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

* Morphology:
(7) الحبك: the plural of حبيكة, which is the path; it is either a noun of a thing or a noun of an idea, i.e. the sensible path or the intelligible path.

safi-cedvel:10-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, an adjective of (الخرّاصون). (في غمرة) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). (ساهون) is a second khabar, nominative. (أيّان) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, an adverb of time attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (يوم), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "when is the coming of the Day of Recompense?"..
And the clause: «قتل الخرّاصون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive and invocatory (duʿāʾiyya).
And the clause: «هم في غمرة» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «يسألون ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from (الخرّاصون).
And the clause: «أيّان يوم الدين» is in the position of the accusative, the direct object of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; and the clause is restricted by the preposition.
13- (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is يأتي (or يجيء). (على النار) is attached to (يفتنون), which is taken to include the meaning "they are exposed", and the (الواو) in (يفتنون) is the deputy agent..
And the clause: «(يجيء) يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «هم على النار يفتنون» is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يفتنون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). 14- (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هذا). (به) is attached to (تستعجلون).
And the clause: «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of an implied saying.
And the clause: «هذا الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «كنتم به تستعجلون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «تستعجلون» is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(الخرّاصون) is the plural of الخرّاص, the intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral خرص, of the bāb of نصر and the bāb of ضرب, meaning "to lie"; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(ساهون) is the plural of ساه, an active participle from the triliteral سها يسهو. ساه underwent ʿilāl by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its pattern is فاع, and the pattern of ساهون is فاعون.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ».
Here the punishment is likened to food that is eaten; then the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi) is omitted, and one of its concomitants is borrowed for it, namely tasting.

safi-cedvel:15-19.t:
* I'rab:
(في جنّات) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (آخذين) is a ḥāl from the pronoun of settledness (istiqrār) which is the khabar of إنّ. (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object of the active participle (آخذين), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what their Lord gave them". (قبل) is an accusative adverb attached to (محسنين)..
Clause: «إنّ المتّقين في جنّات» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «آتاهم ربّهم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «إنّهم كانوا» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason (taʿlīliyya).
And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
17- 18- (قليلا) is an accusative mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, so it is its adjective, attached to (يهجعون) [Note: or an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "little sleeping" ... It may be the khabar of (كان) if (ما) is parsed as a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is then either the agent of (قليلا) or a badal of the ism of كان.]. (من الليل) is attached to an adjective of (قليلا). (ما) is redundant, to stress fewness [Note: or a maṣdar particle ...].. (بالأسحار) is attached to (يستغفرون)..
And the clause: «كانوا (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: or a badal of the clause كانوا ... محسنين, in the position of the nominative.].
And the clause: «يهجعون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of the second كانوا.
And the clause: «هم يستغفرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كانوا (the second).
And the clause: «يستغفرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
19- (الواو) is a conjunction. (في أموالهم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (حقّ). (للسائل) is attached to an adjective of (حقّ), or to (حقّ). And the clause: «في أموالهم حقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كانوا (the second).

* Morphology:
(19) السائل: an active participle from the triliteral سأل, on the pattern فاعل.
(المحروم) is a passive participle from the triliteral حرم, on the pattern مفعول.

safi-cedvel:20-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (في الأرض) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (آيات). (للموقنين) is attached to an adjective of (آيات)..
Clause: «في الأرض آيات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
21- (الواو) is a conjunction. (في أنفسكم) is attached to what (في الأرض) is attached to [Note: or to a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, indicated by the mentioned آيات]. (الهمزة) is for an interrogative of rebuke (istifhām inkārī). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is negative.
And the clause: «لا تبصرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Were you heedless, so that you do not see?"
22- (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (في السّماء) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (رزقكم). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, conjoined to رزقكم, and the (الواو) in (توعدون) is the deputy agent, with the returning pronoun omitted.
And the clause: «في السماء رزقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause في الأرض آيات.
And the clause: «توعدون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
23- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (الواو) is the wāw of the oath. (ربّ) is genitive by the wāw, attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is أقسم. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, giving emphasis; it is a substitute for the shifted lām. (مثل) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in حقّ, accusative [Note: and according to some it is indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, an adjective of حقّ, because it is annexed to an indeclinable word.]. (ما) is an indefinite described noun in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi [Note: or it is redundant, in which case it is good to write it joined to مثل, i.e. مثلما ... and the interpreted maṣdar is the muḍāf ilayhi.].
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم تنطقون ... ) is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو, i.e. "it is your speaking".
And the clause: « (أقسم) بربّ السماء» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause في السماء رزقكم [Note: It may be resumptive.].
And the clause: «انّه لحقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: « (هو) أنّكم تنطقون» is in the position of the genitive, an adjective of (ما).
And the clause: «تنطقون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

* Benefits:
- Allah is the guarantor of provision..
It is related from al-Aṣmaʿī that he said: I came from the Great Mosque of Basra, and a Bedouin appeared on a young camel (the offspring of a camel) and said: "Who is the man?" I said: "From the Banū Aṣmaʿ." He said: "And where are you coming from?"
I said: "From a place where the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic are recited." He said: "Recite to me." So I recited: والذاريات, and when I reached (وَفِي السَّماءِ رِزْقُكُمْ) he said: "Enough for you." He got up to his she-camel, slaughtered it and distributed it to all who came and went, then took his sword and his bow, broke them and departed. When I later made the pilgrimage with al-Rashīd and was performing the circumambulation, there was someone calling to me in a soft voice. I turned, and it was the Bedouin, thin and yellowed. He greeted me and asked me to recite the sūra. When I reached that verse he cried out and said: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true." Then he said: "Is there anything beyond this?" So I recited: (فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق), and he cried out and said: "Glory be to Allah! Who is it that angered the Majestic until He swore? They did not believe Him until He swore." He said it three times, and his soul departed with it.

safi-cedvel:24-30.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is an interrogative particle. (المكرمين) is an adjective of ضيف [Note: it came in the singular form while having the sense of the plural, because it is originally a maṣdar in which singular, dual and plural are alike.]. (إذ) is an adverb of past time in the position of the accusative, attached to (حديث) [Note: or attached to المكرمين, if what is meant is that Ibrāhīm honoured them by serving them ... or it is a noun of time functioning as a direct object of an omitted verb whose implied form is اذكر ("mention").]. (عليه) is attached to (دخلوا). (سلاما) is an absolute object of an omitted verb. (سلام) is a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "peace be upon you". (قوم) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is أنتم or هؤلاء..
Clause: «آتاك حديث ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «دخلوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause دخلوا.
And the clause: « (نسلّم) سلاما ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: « (عليكم) سلام» is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: « (أنتم) قوم» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
26- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (إلى أهله) is attached to (راغ). (بعجل) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of جاء..
And the clause: «راغ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
And the clause: «جاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause راغ.
27- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (إليهم) is attached to (قرّبه). (ألا) is a particle of offering..
And the clause: «قرّبه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause جاء.
And the clause: «قال ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied. And the clause: «ألا تأكلون ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
28- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (منهم) is attached to a ḥāl from خيفة. (خيفة) is an accusative direct object. (لا) is a prohibitive particle that puts the verb in the jussive. (الواو) is circumstantial. (بغلام) is attached to (بشّروه)..
And the clause: «أوجس..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "they did not step forward, so he sensed...".
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «لا تخف ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
And the clause: «بشّروه ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied [Note: or without implying قد.].
29- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (في صرّة) is a ḥāl from امرأته. (عجوز) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is أنا.
And the clause: «أقبلت امرأته ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قالوا.
And the clause: «صكّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أقبلت.
And the clause: «قالت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause صكّت (or أقبلت). And the clause: « (أنا) عجوز ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
30- (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object whose governing element is the following قال [Note: i.e. "Your Lord said a saying like that saying which we have told you of", in the sense that He decreed and judged.]. (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ [Note: It may be borrowed for the position of the accusative, as emphasis of the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ.]. And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «قال ربّك ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.. The object of قال is omitted; it is what كذلك is attached to.
And the clause: «إنّه هو الحكيم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, giving a reason.
And the clause: «هو الحكيم ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(صرّة) is a noun meaning a cry, an uproar, or a group.. It is taken from the triliteral (صرّ); its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa and then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī): in His words, Exalted is He, «هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْراهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ», an interrogative of affirmation, magnifying the importance of the account and alerting that it is not among what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew other than by way of revelation. It is like when you begin to tell someone of something marvellous and ask him whether he has heard it or not: it is as though you expect him to say "No" and ask you to tell it.
2- Omission: in His words, Exalted is He, «قالَ سَلامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ».
It was said: it means "peace be upon you", and he turned it to the nominative by inchoation, intending permanence, so that his greeting would be better than theirs, in a fuller measure of courtesy and honour. And it was said: سلام is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "my affair is «peace»", and «قوم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; most hold that the implied form is "you are an unfamiliar people", and that he, peace be upon him, said it to them in order to get to know them, as you might say to someone you meet: "I do not know you", meaning "tell me who you are and describe yourself".
3- Mursal metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words, Exalted is He, «قالُوا لا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ».
Here the boy is called "knowing" with regard to what his affair will come to when he grows up.

* Benefits:
- The clause that occurs as a direct object..
In this verse occur His words, Exalted is He: فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ. The clause (أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ) is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said.
We shall set out below what relates to the clause occurring as an object:
This clause occurs in three categories:
1- The category of quotation (ḥikāya) or its synonym, as in His words, Exalted is He: قالَ: إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.
2- What is a quoted saying that is implied: His words فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ (وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا): these clauses are in the position of the accusative by agreement; then the Basrans said: the accusative is due to an implied "saying", and the Kufans said: due to the verb mentioned. The Basrans are supported by the explicit mention of the saying in (وَنادى نُوحٌ رَبَّهُ فَقالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي) and (نادى رَبَّهُ نِداءً خَفِيًّا قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي).
3- The category of suspension (taʿlīq): this is the verb's being suspended from seeking its object, in form but not in position, as in His words, Exalted is He: فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً. Suspension is not restricted to the chapter of ظنّ but is particular to every verb of the heart, as in His words, Exalted is He: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا ما بِصاحِبِهِمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ and يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ. Sometimes the clause takes the place of two objects, as in His words, Exalted is He: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً and لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ in the position of the nominative, its khabar being (خطبكم). (أيّها) is an indefinite, specified vocative (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative. (المرسلون) is a badal of أيّ (or an explicative apposition to it), following it in the nominative in form..
Clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «ما خطبكم ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have been sent for some matter, then what is your business?"; and the implied clause is the content of what was said. And the clause: «أيّها المرسلون» has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.

safi-cedvel:32-34.t:
* I'rab:
The pronoun (نا) is the deputy agent of the verb أرسلنا. (إلى قوم) is attached to (أرسلنا)..
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّا أرسلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. And the clause: «أرسلنا ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ. 33- (اللام) is for giving a reason. (نرسل) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (عليهم) is attached to (نرسل). (من طين) is attached to an adjective of (حجارة).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن نرسل ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسلنا). And the clause: «نرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن). 34- (مسوّمة) is a second adjective of حجارة [Note: It may be a ḥāl of حجارة, because it is described by the preposition and its noun.]. (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to (مسوّمة), and likewise (للمسرفين).

safi-cedvel:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (فيها) is attached to the khabar of كان. (من المؤمنين) is attached to a ḥāl from the ism of كان, the returning pronoun. (ما) is negative. (غير) is an accusative direct object. (من المسلمين) is attached to an adjective of (غير) [Note: There is an omitted muḍāf in the speech, i.e. "other than a household of Muslims".]. (الواو) is a conjunction. The second (فيها) is attached to (تركنا). (للذين) is attached to an adjective of (آية)..
Clause: «أخرجنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so they set about what they were commanded, and We brought out whoever was in it..".
And the clause: «كان فيها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun. And the clause: «ما وجدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أخرجنا.
And the clause: «تركنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما وجدنا..
And the clause: «يخافون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(في موسى) is attached to an omitted verb indicated by what is mentioned in the preceding verse, i.e. "We left a sign" [Note: by taking the wāw as resumptive ... It may be conjoined to (فيها) in the preceding verse, in which case the preposition and its noun are attached to the mentioned (تركنا)]. (إذ) is an adverb in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied verb تركنا [Note: or attached to an adjective of آية, i.e. "existing at the time of Our sending ... or attached to آية"]. (إلى فرعون) is attached to (أرسلناه). (بسلطان) is attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (أرسلناه).
Clause: « (تركنا) في موسى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أرسلناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
39- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بركنه) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تولّى [Note: i.e. he turned away, relying on his troops, because troops are to a king like a support (rukn) for him]. (ساحر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو. (أو) is a conjunction. And the clause: «تولّى ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أرسلناه. And the clause: «قال ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تولّى. And the clause: « (هو) ساحر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. 40- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places, and (الواو) likewise [Note: It may be the wāw of accompaniment, with وجنوده a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).]. (جنوده) is conjoined to the pronoun in (أخذناه). (في اليمّ) is attached to (نبذناهم). (الواو) is circumstantial ...
And the clause: «أخذناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تولّى. And the clause: «نبذناهم ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذناه. And the clause: «هو مليم ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the object in (أخذناه) or in (نبذناهم). Part Twenty-seven
The remainder of Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt
From verse 41 to verse 60

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا) is like وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه, in words and clauses [Note: in verse (38) of this sūra]. (عليهم) is attached to (أرسلنا). (ما) is negative. (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (عليه) is attached to (أتت). (إلّا) is for restriction. (كالرميم) is in the place of the second object.
And the clause: «ما تذر ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الريح. And the clause: «أتت عليه» is in the position of the accusative, by position, an adjective of شيء. And the clause: «جعلته ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of تذر [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a second direct object of (تذر), in the sense of "leave", which takes two objects].

* Rhetoric:
Derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ».
It was called barren because it destroyed them and cut off their last remnant; so their destruction and the cutting off of their remnant were likened to the barrenness of women and their not conceiving, because of the loss of offspring in it; then the thing likened to was applied to the thing likened, and العقيم was derived from it.

safi-cedvel:43-45.t:
* I'rab:
«وفي ثمود إذ قيل» is like وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه, in words and clauses [Note: in verse (38) of this sūra.]. (لهم) is attached to (قيل). (حتّى حين) is attached to (تمتّعوا) ...
And the clause: «تمتّعوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, a deputy agent [Note: because it is originally a clause that is the content of what was said]. 44- (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places. (عتوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the (الواو) is the agent. (عن أمر) is attached to (عتوا), which is taken to include the meaning أعرضوا ("they turned away"). (الواو) is circumstantial.
And the clause: «عتوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause قيل. And the clause: «أخذتهم الصاعقة ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause عتوا. And the clause: «هم ينظرون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. And the clause: «ينظرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم). 45- (الفاء) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (قيام) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (ما) is like the first ...
And the clause: «ما استطاعوا....» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذتهم. And the clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذتهم.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (قوم) is a direct object of an omitted verb whose implied form is أهلكنا [Note: or اذكر.]. (قبل) is a noun of adverbial use, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to the implied verb. Clause: « (أهلكنا) قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «إنّهم كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «كانوا قوما ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:47-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (السماء) is a direct object of an omitted verb that is explained by what follows. (بأيد) is a ḥāl from the agent of بنيناها or from its object [Note: or attached to (بنيناها), the باء being causal]; it is genitive by an implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, because of the tanwīn. (الواو) is circumstantial. (اللام) is the shifted lām, giving emphasis..
Clause: « (بنينا) السماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «بنيناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative. And the clause: «إنّا لموسعون ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl ...
48- (الواو) is a conjunction. (الأرض) is like السماء. (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. نحن ("We").
And the clause: « (فرشنا) الأرض» ... ) has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause (بنينا). And the clause: «فرشناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative. And the clause: «نعم الماهدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (فرشنا). 49- (الواو) is a conjunction. (من كلّ) is attached to (خلقنا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from زوجين, an adjective that has been fronted before the described noun]. (تذكّرون) is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs was dropped ...
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause (فرشنا). And the clause: «لعلّكم تذكّرون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «تذكّرون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of لعلّ. 50- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (إلى الله) is attached to (فرّوا), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "to the reward of Allah". (لكم) is attached to (نذير). (منه) is attached to a ḥāl from نذير.
And the clause: «فرّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied condition ..., i.e. "if you have known the attributes of Allah mentioned, then flee to Him". And the clause: «انّي لكم منه نذير ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. 51- (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is a prohibitive particle that puts the verb in the jussive. (مع) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted second direct object. (إنّي لكم ... ) is like the first. And the clause: «لا تجعلوا ... » is conjoined to the clause فرّوا. And the clause: «إنّي لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(48) الماهدون: the plural of الماهد, an active participle from the triliteral مهد; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
Ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb)..
In this verse occur His words, Exalted is He: وَالسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ. السماء is accusative by ishtighāl. We shall set out below what relates to this topic:
Ishtighāl is when something that is an object in meaning is fronted before a governing element that has put the pronoun of this object in the accusative, such as (دارك رأيتها, "your house, I saw it"), or has put in the accusative something connected with its pronoun, such as (دارك طرقت بابها, "your house, I knocked on its door") and (أخاك مررت به, "your brother, I passed by him"). Were it not that the governing element is occupied with putting the pronoun, or what is connected with it, in the accusative, it would have put the fronted noun itself in the accusative. So they imply for this accusative noun a governing element of the same form as the mentioned verb, or of its meaning if it is intransitive. Thus the governing element in the second example is an omitted (طرقت), and in the last example it is from the meaning of the mentioned verb and not from its form, because it is an intransitive verb, and its implied form is (جاوزت أخاك مررت به).
In the preceding examples it is also permissible to put the fronted noun in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the clause after it as its khabar, so you say: (دارك رأيتها), (دارك طرقت بابها), (أخوك مررت به).
a- The accusative of the noun that the verb is occupied away from is obligatory when it occurs after what is particular to verbs, such as particles of condition and of urging, and particles of interrogation other than the hamza. Between this noun and what precedes it an omitted verb is implied obligatorily, so that the particle remains attached to what it is particular to, such as: (إن محمدا لقيته فأكرمه), (هلا فقيرا أطعمته), (متى أخاك لقيته), (هل الكتاب قرأته). The governing element mentioned after it then serves as an explanation of the omitted one.
b- The accusative is preferred in three places:
1- When it comes before a verb indicating a request, such as (الفقير أكرمه).
2- After the interrogative hamza, because the verb usually follows it: such as (أجارك تؤذيه؟).
3- When it heads the answer to a question, in the accusative. For example someone asks you: "What do you eat?"
You say: (رغيفا آكله).

safi-cedvel:52-55.t:
* I'rab:
(كذلك) is attached to an omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter (or the case) is thus". (ما) is negative. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative noun. (رسول) is genitive in form and nominative in position, the agent of أتى. (إلّا) is for restriction. (ساحر) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو. (أو) is a conjunction ...
Clause: « (الأمر) كذلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «ما أتى ... من رسول» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «قالوا ... » is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the relative noun. And the clause: « (هو) ساحر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the content of what was said. 53- (الهمزة) is for an interrogative of rebuke. (تواصوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (به) is attached to (تواصوا). (بل) is for a transitional turning-away (iḍrāb intiqālī)..
And the clause: «تواصوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «هم قوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. 54- 55- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (عنهم) is attached to (تولّ). (الفاء) gives a reason. (ما) is negative, working like ليس. (ملوم) is genitive in form by the باء and accusative in position, the khabar of ما ... (الواو) is resumptive. (الفاء) gives a reason..
And the clause: «تولّ ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not respond to you, then turn away from them". And the clause: «ما أنت بملوم» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «ذكّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: It is said that this verse abrogates the preceding verse, "turn away from them ...", being revealed some time after the revelation of the first verse]. And the clause: «إن الذكرى تنفع ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason. And the clause: «تنفع ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(53) تواصوا: it has ʿilāl by deletion. The alif, the lām (final radical) of the word, was deleted because it met the wāw of the plural while quiescent, and what precedes the wāw remained with fatḥa to indicate the omitted alif; its pattern is تفاعوا.

* Benefits:
- The clause that occurs as a khabar..
The clause that occurs as a khabar is among the clauses that have a grammatical position. It is a khabar for three things:
1- A khabar for the mubtadaʾ, its position being the nominative, such as: (الله يعلم الغيب, "Allah knows the unseen") or (العلم كنوزه ثمينة, "knowledge, its treasures are precious").
2- A khabar for (إن) or one of its sisters, its position also being the nominative, as in His words, Exalted is He, in the verse we are concerned with: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ, or (إن البحر ركوبه خطير, "the sea, riding it is dangerous").
3- A khabar for the defective verb (كان and its sisters) or (كاد and its sisters), its position being the accusative, such as His words, Exalted is He: فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلى ما أَنْفَقَ فِيها and وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ.

safi-cedvel:56-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما) is negative. (إلّا) is for restriction. (اللام) is for giving a reason. (يعبدون) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām ... and the (النون) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which was omitted to suit the verse-ending.
Clause: «ما خلقت ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. And the clause: «يعبدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعبدون ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (خلقت). 57- (ما) is negative. (منهم) is attached to (أريد). (رزق) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a direct object. (ما أريد) is like the first. (يطعمون) is like يعبدون, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يطعمون) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object, its governing element being أريد. And the clause: «ما أريد (the first)» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption. And the clause: «ما أريد (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the first clause أريد. 58- (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الرزاق.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ]. (الرزاق) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative. (ذو) is a second khabar, nominative [Note: or an adjective of الرزاق]. (المتين) is a third khabar [Note: or an adjective of (ذو). Or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is هو, and the clause is resumptive, confirming the content of what preceded]. And the clause: «إنّ الله ... الرزاق» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.

* Morphology:
(58) الرزّاق: an intensive form from the triliteral رزق; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn. (58) المتين: a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from (متن) of the bāb of كرم, meaning hard and strong; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:59-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links the response to an implied condition in both places. (للذين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (مثل) is an adjective of (ذنوبا), accusative. (لا) is prohibitive, and the (النون) in (يستعجلون) is the nūn of protection before the first-person yāʾ, which was omitted to suit the verse-ending..
Clause: «إنّ للذين ظلموا ذنوبا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the earlier nations had a share of punishment, then those who did wrong among the disbelievers of Mecca have a share like theirs". And the clause: «ظلموا..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). And the clause: «لا يستعجلون» is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if I delay their punishment, then let them not hasten Me". 60- (الفاء) links the response to an implied condition. (ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: an indefinite noun that carries a sense of reproach, so beginning with it is valid]. (للذين) is attached to an omitted element, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ويل. (من يومهم) is attached to the maṣdar (ويل), and the wāw in (يوعدون) is the deputy agent.
And the clause: «ويل للذين ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the time of their punishment (or the day of their punishment) comes, then woe to them". And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). And the clause: «يوعدون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(ذنوب) is a noun meaning a bucket with a tail, or a grave; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa and then ḍamma.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His words, Exalted is He, «فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوباً مِثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحابِهِمْ».
الذنوب: the large bucket. This is a representation, whose origin is in water-drawers dividing the water, so that this one has a bucket and that one has a bucket. He said:
لنا ذنوب ولكم ذنوب ... فإن أبيتم فلنا القليب
(We have a bucketful and you have a bucketful; if you refuse, then the well is ours.)
The meaning: those of the people of Mecca who wronged the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by denial have a share of Allah's punishment, like the share of their fellows and peers among the earlier generations.
